title: Minnesota lawyer suspended over fake AI case citations

reading.body:
An attorney used an AI tool to generate case citations while drafting a legal brief and submitted citations to two cases that did not exist. The fabricated citations appeared in a civil dispute over unpaid rent in Hennepin County Court. The false citations were discovered during a hearing when opposing counsel raised the issue with the judge.

This is a model failure where the AI system generated plausible-sounding but entirely false legal authorities. The failure occurred in deployment without adequate human verification of the citations before submission to the court. A lawyer reviewing the cited cases in a legal database before filing would have caught the fabrications.

It is not established whether the attorney was aware the AI could generate false citations, or whether he understood the risks of using AI for this purpose.

reports.title: Minnesota lawyer suspended over fake AI case citations

summary:
Minnesota attorney Faisal S. Ahmed submitted a legal brief in Hennepin County Court containing citations to two cases that never existed. He cited Anderson v. City of Biwabik and Doherty v. Alma E. Clark Memorial Home to support arguments in a civil case involving a food store owner being sued by his landlord for unpaid rent. Ahmed generated these fake cases using an AI tool while drafting the memorandum. The fabricated citations were discovered during an August hearing when opposing counsel George Warner Jr. informed the judge that the brief likely contained AI hallucinations.

Judge Lois Conroy ruled against Ahmed's client and ordered payment of $233,563 in back rent. She fined Ahmed $5,000 and referred him to the Minnesota Lawyer's Professional Responsibility Board. Following an investigation, Ahmed agreed to accept a 30-day suspension of his law license and pay an additional $900 in costs. This incident is part of a growing problem, with over 800 documented cases of litigants using AI to fabricate legal citations and quotes.
